Running head across top centred under an ornamental border: "DVODECIM PSALMI DA-" continuing into "VIDIS, AB ANONYMO QVO-" (two lines, the second in spaced capitals). Main text in one column: an introductory paragraph, then a centred heading "PSALMVS 1." with its argument line, then numbered verses 1 to 5 with a historiated initial O at verse 1. page.running_head: DVODECIM PSALMI DAVIDIS, AB ANONYMO QVODAM

main_text.p: VIDIS, AB ANONYMO QVODAM, poeta elegantiss. vario carminum genere pene ad verbum, & admodum felicitèr expressi.
main_text.head: PSALMVS 1. Constat sex versibus Hebraeis, totidem Latinis.
main_text.p: 1. OVI recto graditur calle beatus est: Nec stat nequitiæ præcipiti in via, Nec sella petulãs pestifera sedet, Cuius iniciens notam:
2. Sed totus Domini dogmata ruminat Ac præcepta Dei cogitat & facit, Quem nox sollicitum, lux videt anxium Addictum studijs piis.
3. Talis vir rigua par erit arbori Quæ non deciduis floribus effluit, Sed plantata secus flumina germinat, Et fructus gerit veres.
4. E contra reprobi quisquiliæ velut, Aut gluma à rabido turbine concita, Infestans oculos pulvis inutilis Trita pellitur area.

page.notes: Printed text is set in roman with italic and some letters in a decorative style. The verse text is quoted in italic. Marginal fragments in the right margin (partial letters and numbers, such as "6." and "7.", and a stray mark) are cut off and illegible, so they are omitted. The page ends mid-psalm: verse 5 continues on the next page. Verse 1 begins with a historiated initial "O" joined to "VI". The Hebrew verse count is stated in the argument line. Several words in the verses are set with unusual letter forms and may be misread: "Nec stat" and "sella" in verse 1, "iniciens" in verse 1, "rigua" and "veres" in verse 3, "quisquiliæ" in verse 4. Marked words are not individually flagged with [?] because the scan is clear enough for these readings, but they should be checked against the original.
